Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test does:
  - testSevenEmptyFiles delegates to testCompress252(7, 0). That helper:
    - Opens a SevenZOutputFile.
    - Adds a directory entry "foo/".
    - Adds 7 file entries "foo/0.txt" … "foo/6.txt".
    - For this test, all 7 files are empty: addFile writes new byte[0], then closes the entry.
  - The directory entry is created via createArchiveEntry(dir, "foo/") and is flagged as a directory.

- How entries are recorded during writing:
  - putArchiveEntry simply adds the SevenZArchiveEntry to an internal files list.
  - closeArchiveEntry inspects whether any data was written for the current entry:
    - If fileBytesWritten > 0: it marks the entry as having a stream (hasStream=true), sets sizes and CRCs, and increments numNonEmptyStreams.
    - Otherwise (empty entry): it explicitly marks hasStream=false and sizes 0. This applies to the directory and all 7 files in this test.

- Where the failure comes from:
  - When closing the archive, SevenZOutputFile writes the 7z header. Part of the header’s FilesInfo section is a compact bitset that marks which entries “have a stream” (and related flags for empty streams and directories). These boolean vectors are encoded bitwise in bytes (8 flags per byte) as mandated by the 7z format.
  - In this scenario, the total number of file entries is 8 (1 directory + 7 empty files). This hits a boundary condition: exactly one full byte of bits is needed for the boolean vector.
  - Due to a bug in the header encoding logic for these boolean vectors, the final byte is not emitted when the number of entries is an exact multiple of 8 (or the flush logic is otherwise off-by-one). As a result, the EmptyStreams/HasStream mask is truncated.
  - With the mask corrupted, the reader (7-Zip/Commons) misinterprets the FilesInfo metadata. A common symptom is that the archive appears to contain only a single folder entry (often with the name of the archive itself), exactly as described in the bug report.
  - This explains the threshold “more than 7 files”: at 8 entries (here 1 dir + 7 files), the bitset boundary triggers the bug. With fewer than 8 entries, the partial byte is flushed and the archive is correct.

- Why the test reliably reproduces it:
  - The test constructs precisely 8 entries with 0 non-empty streams: 1 directory and 7 empty files.
  - closeArchiveEntry correctly marks them as hasStream=false, so the header must rely entirely on the boolean vectors to represent the files.
  - The defective bitset emission for exactly-one-byte cases corrupts the metadata, leading to the observed “single folder entry” result and failing verification.

In short, the archive-writing path correctly sets each entry as empty, but the header’s boolean-vector encoding has an off-by-one/flush bug when the number of entries is a multiple of 8, corrupting the FilesInfo section for the “7 empty files” case (plus directory), which manifests as a broken archive.
